previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a 58-year-old male with AML status post double cord blood transplant, was admitted with acute respiratory distress and found to have ARDS. Initial treatment included intubation and broad-spectrum antibiotics, but infectious workup was negative. Imaging and clinical course supported a diagnosis of bronchiolitis obliterans organizing pneumonia (BOOP), leading to initiation of high-dose steroids with gradual taper. He experienced transient facial numbness, likely due to hypotension, with normal neuroimaging. Acute kidney injury, attributed to cyclosporine toxicity, resolved with dose reduction. He developed steroid-induced hyperglycemia requiring insulin. Coronary artery disease was identified via CT, with normal stress test but mildly reduced ejection fraction. He was weaned from mechanical ventilation, transitioned to oral prednisone, and discharged to pulmonary rehab on a regimen including immunosuppressants, antifungals, and cardiac medications.

HISTORY:  Status post bone marrow transplant, now with pain in the tib-fib
region and bilateral toe erythema.

FINDINGS:  No previous images.  Two views of the leg and three of the foot
show no evidence of acute bone or joint space abnormality.  Minimal calcaneal
spurs seen inferiorly and posteriorly.  No convincing evidence of bone erosion
to suggest osteomyelitis.

CHEST RADIOGRAPH

INDICATION:  Increased edema.

COMPARISON:  ___.

FINDINGS:  Unchanged position of the central venous access line.  Moderate
cardiomegaly without signs of overhydration.  Relatively wide mediastinum, but
without pathological contours.  No evidence of pleural effusions on the
frontal or lateral radiograph.  At the dorsal, basal lungs, there is a very
subtle peribronchial thickening that could correspond to either subtle
pneumonia or minimal fluid retention.  No other parenchymal abnormalities.

HISTORY:  ___ male with history of AML, presenting with right lower
extremity pain and erythema concerning for DVT.

COMPARISON:  Bilateral lower extremity venous ultrasound of ___.

RIGHT LOWER EXTREMITY VENOUS ULTRASOUND:  Gray-scale and color and duplex
Doppler ultrasound evaluation was performed over the left common femoral vein
as well as the right common femoral, superficial femoral, and popliteal veins.
There is normal flow, augmentation, and compressibility.  No evidence of
intraluminal thrombus is seen.

Note is made of induration of the superficial soft tissues over the right calf
region.

IMPRESSION:  No evidence of DVT seen in the right lower extremity.

INDICATION:  ___ man with acute renal failure.

Comparison is made to the prior renal ultrasound performed on ___.

FINDINGS:  The right kidney measures 11.6 and the left kidney measures 12.8
cm.  No stone, mass, or hydronephrosis in the kidneys.  The partially full
bladder has normal appearance.

IMPRESSION:  No hydronephrosis.
